_comment: The Map of the Future. Derived from roughly 900 KB of research into the Moonshots archive and related channels, August 2026. Part A is the raw thematic list, uncurated. Part B is what survives a filter of: one person, home hardware, near-zero capital, and not already a bloodbath. No dates anywhere, deliberately. It is a map, not a schedule.

source.corpus: ~900 KB of research summaries drawn from Moonshots with Peter Diamandis and related channels, not raw transcripts
source.taxonomy: The 24-Branch System, revision 6, dated 2026-08-18, credited to Gemini Notebook

part_b.title: What one person could actually build
filter: One person, home hardware. Nothing here needs serious local compute; anything model-heavy calls a hosted API.
No lab equipment, no manufacturing, no regulatory approval pathway, no physical supply chain.
Not already saturated by well-funded competitors.
A narrow, identifiable buyer. Not everyone. A specific small population with this exact problem now.

top_pick.name: Citation and reference integrity checker
top_pick.why_now: The problem I hit twice in the conversation that produced this list. AI research assistants fabricate specific-sounding citations, episode numbers, guest names, dates and URLs that do not survive a check against the real source. My own 900 KB research corpus is full of it: invented episode numbers, claims attributed to episodes that may not say what is claimed.
top_pick.what_it_does: Paste in a document. It extracts every citation-shaped claim and checks it against real public metadata, podcast feeds, video APIs, publisher sites, then flags each one CONFIRMED, MISMATCHED where the source exists but does not say that, or NOT FOUND where the source does not appear to exist at all.
top_pick.why_it_clears: Near-zero capital on free public APIs. Narrow enough not to compete with AxiomTEA, which does physics rather than citations, or with general fact-checkers, which do political truth rather than source existence. The buyer is concrete and growing: anyone using AI for research who has been burned by exactly this. And the test corpus already exists, for free, in my own files.

candidates.name: Prediction ledger and forecaster track record
candidates.what: A structured record of specific dated predictions by public figures, with target dates, and an ongoing scorecard of what came true.
candidates.different_from: Metaculus and Manifold are crowd markets on open questions going forward. This is retrospective and person-specific.
candidates.risk: More labour to seed than the top pick. Predictions have to be found and dated correctly by hand at first.

candidates.name: Hype-density self-check for writers
candidates.what: AxiomTEA's unfalsifiable-claim-density idea pointed at a different buyer: writers checking their own draft before publishing, framed as craft rather than a verdict.
candidates.risk: Willingness to pay for making your own writing more credible is genuinely unproven and would need validating early.

candidates.name: Session-prep compiler
candidates.what: Takes loose campaign notes and compiles them into a consistent prep document matching an established style and canon, catching continuity contradictions rather than rules violations.
candidates.risk: Thin moat. World Anvil, LegendKeeper and Notion templates already cover part of this. Listed as a real option, not a strong one.

candidates.name: Token cost and API usage audit for solo developers
candidates.what: Ingests billing exports and flags waste: redundant calls, oversized context windows, repeated identical prompts, with concrete fixes.
candidates.risk: The providers already ship dashboards. The differentiator would have to be genuinely sharper waste detection, not another cost graph.
